**1\. Title, goal statement and conventions**

**Project title:** Ad-Vocates

**Team Members:** Dylan Shackleford, Max Marsh

**Goal:** Create a reliable and efficient tool that improves browsing performance while giving users greater privacy, security, and control over their web experience.

**Conventions:** Solid boxes represent components built by the team, circles represent external dependencies the team does not build, arrows for the D0 diagram represent interfaces, arrows for the data-flow diagram represent data with its form labeled

**Basic input:** Browser request data, user protection settings and filter rules from approved sources

**Basic output:** Block/allow output, and dashboard showing blocked requests and estimated data saved

**3\. Component responsibility table**

| Component | Interface in/out | Primary owner | User story |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Dashboard \- present controls, settings and statistics to user | In : None Out: I5, I6 | Max Marsh | US-02, 03, 05 |
| Settings \- manage filters and protection settings | In: I6, I10 Out: I7, I11 | Max Marsh | US-03, 04, 05 |
| Statistic Recorder \- produce diagnostic stats from blocking event data | In: I3, I5 Out: I4 | Dylan Shackleford | US-01, 02 |
| Filter Request \- block or allow browser request based on filters/settings | In: I1, I11 Out: I2, I3 | Max Marsh | US-01, 03, 05 |
| Local Storage \- persistent app records stored on user machine | In: I2, I4, I7 Out: None | Max Marsh | US-02, 03, 04, 05 |
| Filter Updater \- fetch updated/current filter data from approved sources | In: None Out: I8, I9 | Dylan Shackleford | US-04 |
| Filter Validator \- validate safety of retrieved filter set | In: I9 Out: I0 | Dylan Shackleford | US-04 |

**4\. Interface specification table**

| ID | Named and typed in/out | Data format | Protocol | Error behavior / handler |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| I1 | Browser to Filter Request | In : requestId: string, requestUrl: string, resourceType: string, pageHost: string Out: result: enum(allowed, blocked) | Structured object | Browser extension request | Filter Request allows request if filtering fails and tries to log error in Local Storage |
| I2 | Filter Request to Local Storage | In: action: enum(readFilters, logError), errorMsg: string (opt) Out: filters: string\[\], status: enum(success, failed) | JSON | Local read/write | Filter Request keeps current filters if read fails, if log fails filtering continues  |
| I3 | Filter Request to Statistic Recorder | In: eventId : string, category : enum(ad, tracker, redirect, other), estimatedBytes: int  Out: None | JSON | Local internal event | Statistic Recorder ignores duplicate events and continues if recording fails |
| I4 | Statistic Recorder to Local Storage | In: action: enum(read, write), blockedTotal : int (opt), estimatedBytes: int (opt) Out: blockedTotal: int, estimatedBytes: int, status: enum(success, failed) | JSON | Local read/write | Statistic Recorder keeps current total in memory if save fails and reports unavailable statistics if read fails |
| I5 | Dashboard to Statistic Recorder | In: query: enum(getTotal) Out: blockedTotal : int, estimatedBytes: int, status: enum(success, failed) | JSON | Local query/response | Dashboard shows “Statistics currently unavailable” if query fails |
| I6 | Dashboard to Settings | In: action: enum(read,write), enabled: bool (opt), allowlist: string\[\] (opt) Out: enabled: bool, allowlist: string\[\], status: enum(success, failed) | JSON | Local request/response | Settings rejects invalid addresses, keeps prior config, and returns error to Dashboard |
| I7 | Settings to Local Storage | In: action: enum(read,write), enabled: bool (opt), allowlist: string\[\] (opt), filters: string\[\] (opt) Out: enabled: bool, allowlist: string\[\], filters: string\[\], status: enum(success,  failed) | JSON | Local read/write | Settings keeps prior config if save fails and reports failure through Dashboard |
| I8  | Filter Updater to Approved Sources | In: sourceUrl: string Out: filterText: string, statusCode: int | Plain text filter | HTTPS request | Filter Updater retries a set amount of hours later if download fails and keeps existing filters |
| I9 | Filter Updater to Filter Validator | In: sourceUrl: string, filterText: string Out: valid: bool, errorMsg: string (opt) | Structured object | Local validation request/response | Filter Validator rejects unapproved sources or invalid filters, existing filters stay active |
| I10 | Filter Validator to Settings | In: filters: string\[\] Out: status: enum(success,failed) | JSON | Local request/response | Settings keeps previous filters if new validated filters cannot be saved/applied |
| I11 | Settings to Filter Request | In: enabled: bool, allowlist: string\[\], filters: string\[\] Out: status: enum(success,failed) | JSON | Local request/response | Filter Request keeps previous config if new config fails, Settings reports error to Dashboard |

An example payload for I3 would be the following:  
{  
  “eventId”: “request1”,  
  “category”: “ad”,  
  “estimatedBytes”: 1234  
}

**6\. Architecture pattern and justification**

Ad-Vocates uses layered, pipeline, and client-server architecture. 

The main application utilizes the layered pattern. The Dashboard serves as the presentation layer, with the application components handling functions, and Local Storage handling saved data. This matches the layered pattern of separating the presentation, logic, and data aspects of an application. 

The pipeline pattern is utilized for the filter updating functionality. When filters are downloaded, they must move through the Filter Updater, Filter Validator, and Settings components before they will be used for filtering. 

The client-server pattern is utilized for the download functionality of the Filter Updater. Ad-Vocates acts as a client, requesting a filter list from an approved source, and downloads the data from an external server.

These patterns were chosen because of the following criteria:

**Fit to the problem:** This architecture is fit to the problem, since these patterns match the way that the system works. The layered pattern separates the user interface, application functions and filtering logic, and storage which fits the desired design of the ad-blocker application. The pipeline pattern fits the process created to update filters, following a multi-step download and validation pipeline prior to allowing filters to be used. The client-server pattern is also a fitting pattern for governing the downloading of the filters from external approved sources. 

**Team skills:** For a small, two-person team, these patterns fit well since they are not too complex to be handled by a small team size. As well, they create clear division in the components and architecture of the application, allowing for clean division of work and priority among the two members. 

**Performance and timing:** Local filtering is used so requests can be processed quickly, and statistic reporting is separate from the filtering process to ensure quick processing of requests.

**Scalability:** Since Ad-Vocates is ran locally for each user, adding more users does not cause a server-strain issue, making scalability more practical.

**Hardware constraints:** Ad-Vocates will run on a user’s machine and should consume little resources of the user’s machine.

One pattern which was rejected was the microservices pattern. The reason why this pattern was rejected was because Ad-Vocates is not a large enough project to warrant the use of a microservice architecture. This architecture would be too complex and add little value to this type of project, and is more suitable for large systems.

**7\. Decision log**

| Decision | Alternatives considered | Reasoning for choice |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Filtering is performed locally. | Sending requests to a remote filtering server. | Local filtering avoids network trip and keeps browsing information on the device. |
| The Filter Updater and Filter Validator will be separate. | One component downloads and checks filters. | A single component handling downloading and validation would be too much responsibility for a single component. |
| Statistics will collect blocked totals rather than browsing history data. | Save individual browsing requests | Gathering totals of blocked counts provided the information the Dashboard needs to present statistics, while reducing the information collected. |
| Use a website allowlist within settings | Pop-ups to allow individual websites, disable protection fully | Allowing the user to create their own allowlist can let users access websites broken by filtering in a flexible manner. Pop-ups lack persistence, and fully disabled protection increases risk for users and creates a weaker ad-blocker. |
